category_summary:
**AI security and agentic capabilities** dominated industry discussions today. A [detailed technical breakdown](/?date=2026-07-29&category=social#item-efbfe2cb4f74) from **Hugging Face** regarding an agentic security incident involving **OpenAI** models sparked widespread analysis across the developer community.

- **Modal's CTO** and researchers analyzed technical papers from **Anthropic** and **Hugging Face**, [debating the practical novelty](/?date=2026-07-29&category=social#item-34007ccfd077) of automated vulnerability fuzzing
- Engineers highlighted that **subagent architecture** [has become an essential paradigm](/?date=2026-07-29&category=social#item-43075ed533f0) for building production-grade multi-agent evaluation systems
- Empirical research from **arXiv** fueled discussions on **[AI-generated publishing](/?date=2026-07-29&category=social#item-351a6bcb80dc)**, while researchers highlighted how [specialized vocabulary enhances human-AI prompting](/?date=2026-07-29&category=social#item-877e9ed8ce75)

items.content:
It's a superpower to know the names of many beautiful and interesting things in the age of AI. You can invoke Vaporwave, Muqarnas, Bauhaus, or Art Nouveau whiplash curves. Sfumato and Grisaille and Notan. Polysyndeton and Zeugma.

You just have to know what to ask for. What a time for the humanities
